explanation: Scan left to right while mapping each previous value to its index. Look up target minus the current value before inserting it, which prevents reusing the same position.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time for n values. Each position performs one complement lookup and one insertion, with expected constant-time hashing.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. The map retains at most one index per distinct value.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 Python algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: Before index i, the map contains only earlier positions. A found complement therefore supplies a distinct position with the required sum. Every valid pair is discovered when its later position is processed; the unique-pair promise makes that returned witness sufficient.
walkthrough: For nums=[12,3,8,4] and target=7, record 12,3 and 8 as their positions pass. At index 3, the complement of 4 is 3, already recorded at index 1. Return [1,3]; those two different positions sum to 7.
edgeCases: Equal values may form a pair when they occur at two different indices.
Lookup happens before insertion, preventing reuse of the current position.
Negative values use the same complement equation.
